newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends lower, slow downtrend seen.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends lower, slow downtrend seen.

text.p: Quarter-end U.S. dollar demand and continued foreign fund outflows pulled the Taiwan dollar to a lower close on Friday, and dealers said the local currency's slowly depreciating trend remained largely unchanged.
The local unit finished at T$27.888 against Thursday's T$27.880 close.
Turnover through dealers was US$189 million.
The U.S. dollar's rebound overseas also strengthened the Taiwan dollar's downtrend, dealers said.
"All factors indicate the Taiwan dollar remains in a depreciating trend," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The central bank was expected to continue actions to blunt any volatile depreciation.
"The problem is the central bank has made clear it wants a slow Taiwan dollar depreciation," the dealer said. "The central bank always gets what it wants."
A narrow range of T$27.87-89 range was seen for Saturday.
